method: Primary classical texts/translations plus NASA for separate astronomical facts. Original Hindi teaching, original hypothetical partial charts and arithmetic. Source summaries brief; no verbatim verse invention, no case histories, no guaranteed future. Source table distinguishes text, commentary and original teaching.

sources.title: Phaladeepika, V. Subrahmanya Sastri translation, chapter 10, verses 12–14
supported_claims: Verse 13 treats dasha periods of planets occupying, aspecting or owning the seventh in marriage timing.
Verses 12 and 14 also discuss transit conditions; verse 14 includes strength and rasi/navamsa references.
sources.verification: Read chapter text at verse 12–14. OCR caveat retained. Did not adopt deterministic historical predictions elsewhere in the chapter.

sources.title: Phaladeepika, chapter 20, verse 1 and chapter context
supported_claims: Chapter introduction distinguishes results of strong and weak bhava lords and the timing of their results.
sources.verification: Read chapter introduction. Original workflow is identified as teaching synthesis, not a verbatim classical rule.

sources.title: Brihat Jataka 2.13, Sanskrit and Michael D Neely translation
supported_claims: Verse provides increasing quarter aspects and special aspect roles for Saturn, Jupiter and Mars.
The lesson uses the standard introductory full-aspect convention: all seven seventh; Mars fourth/eighth, Jupiter fifth/ninth, Saturn third/tenth in addition.
sources.verification: Read displayed Sanskrit, translation and grammar breakdown; no Sanskrit verse was invented or reproduced.

sources.title: Phaladeepika chapter 15, verses 1–2
supported_claims: Bhava assessment distinguishes own-lord influence and different planet associations or aspects.
Mixed support and affliction lead to mixed consideration rather than a one-factor judgment.
sources.verification: Read verses 1–2; concise source summary shared between two articles. Detailed worked charts and interpretive questions are original.

sources.title: Phaladeepika chapter 18, verses 1–5
supported_claims: The chapter describes conjunctions by planetary pairs.
The closing direction at verse 5 extends pairwise consideration to more than two planets.
sources.verification: Read verses 1–5. Harsh character stereotypes, deterministic social judgments and close paraphrase of specific pair predictions were excluded.

sources.title: Phaladeepika chapter 4, verses 4, 7 and 9
supported_claims: Verses 4 and 7 discuss loss of strength when rays are overpowered by the Sun, within a broader chapter on multiple kinds of strength.
Verse 9 discusses seventh-aspect importance and acknowledges a view that the special aspects are fully effective.
sources.verification: Read displayed text for exact cited verses; source summaries remain short, while examples are original. No claim that entire total strength becomes mathematically zero solely from combustion.

sources.title: NASA Basics of Space Flight chapter 1, Inferior and Superior Planets and conjunction definitions
supported_claims: Mercury and Venus appear near the Sun from Earth, owing to their inner orbits.
Elongation concerns the apparent angle from the Sun.
Mercury and Venus can have inferior and superior conjunctions; apparent solar conjunction is not physical collision or destruction.
sources.verification: Read relevant section at lines 370–378. Used only for astronomy; not cited as empirical support for astrology.

sources.title: Saravali, R. Santhanam translation/commentary, Volume II, chapter 36 commentary, printed pages 676–677
supported_claims: Commentary table on printed p.677 lists Mercury combustion area 14 degrees direct, 12 degrees retrograde.
Same table lists Venus 10 degrees direct, 8 degrees retrograde.
Note specifies plus or minus with respect to Sun longitude.
Printed pp.676–677 exempt Venus and Saturn from combustion-related reduction within the particular ray calculation context; this is not a universal exemption from consideration.
sources.verification: Search service retrieved the PDF result but opening failed because size exceeded service limit. Downloaded the identified 11,749,495-byte, 485-page PDF via Python; rendered local PDF pages 315 and 316 and visually read the original page images, which show printed pp.676–677. Used only Mercury/Venus threshold rows. Clearly labeled these as translator commentary, not a numbered original Sanskrit verse. No quotations copied.

example_constraints: 55: Four-planet partial Taurus chart; Venus–Mars and Saturn–Mars dasha combinations explicitly assumed for exercises, never calculated without Moon data. No calendar year or real transit claim.
46: Three outer-planet partial Aries chart, aspect direction and inclusive counts checked.
45: Only Mercury and Venus positions assigned in Virgo; no Sun longitude assumed, hence no combustion verdict. Degree comparison exercises preserve physical possibility.

49: Virgo Sun 20°, Mercury 13°, Leo Venus 28°; shortest longitude differences 7° and 22°, plausible inner-planet elongations; both planets explicitly assumed direct. Threshold classification uses only visually verified Mercury/Venus rows.
All charts: whole-sign houses match sign and lagna; examples are not actual birth epochs.
